content: Homage to that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Fully Awakened BuddhaThere are six descriptions – the description of the aggregates, the description of the bases, the description of the elements, the description of the truths, the description of the faculties, and the description of persons.What does the description of the aggregates cover? It covers the five aggregates – the aggregate of material form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, and the aggregate of consciousness; that is what the description of the aggregates covers.What does the description of the bases cover? It covers the twelve bases – the eye base, the visible-form base, the ear base, the sound base, the nose base, the smell base, the tongue base, the taste base, the body base, the tangible base, the mind base, and the mind-object base; that is what the description of the bases covers.What does the description of the elements cover? It covers the eighteen elements – the eye element, the visible-form element, the eye-consciousness element, the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, the nose element, the smell element, the nose-consciousness element, the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, the body element, the tangible element, the body-consciousness element, the mind-element, the mind-object element, and the mind-consciousness element; that is what the description of the elements covers.What does the description of the truths cover? It covers the four truths – the truth of suffering, the truth of its origin, the truth of its ending, and the truth of the path; that is what the description of the truths covers.What does the description of the faculties cover? It covers the twenty-two faculties – the eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, the mind faculty, the femininity faculty, the masculinity faculty, the life faculty, the pleasure faculty, the suffering faculty, the joy faculty, the displeasure faculty, the equanimity faculty, the faith faculty, the energy faculty, the mindfulness faculty, the concentration faculty, the wisdom faculty, the faculty of "I shall know what is not yet known", the faculty of final knowledge, and the faculty of one who has fully known; that is what the description of the faculties covers.What does the description of persons cover?(1) One liberated at times(2) One liberated regardless of times(3) One whose attainments can be shaken(4) One whose attainments cannot be shaken(5) One liable to fall away(6) One not liable to fall away(7) One able to hold on through volition(8) One able to hold on through guarding(9) An ordinary person(10) One who enters the lineage(11) One who refrains out of fear(12) One who refrains without fear(13) One able to progress(14) One unable to progress(15) One whose destiny is fixed(16) One whose destiny is not fixed(17) One who is practising(18) One established in the fruit(19) One whose two ends come at once(20) One for whom the aeon remains(21) A noble one(22) One who is not noble(23) A learner(24) An adept(25) One who is neither a learner nor an adept(26) One with the three knowledges(27) One with the six direct knowledges(28) A Fully Awakened Buddha(29) A Solitary Buddha [variant: paccekabuddho (Sī.)](30) One liberated both ways(31) One liberated by wisdom(32) A body-witness(33) One attained to view(34) One liberated by faith(35) A follower by the teaching(36) A follower by faith(37) One with at most seven more lives(38) One who goes from family to family(39) One with a single seed(40) A once-returner(41) A non-returner(42) One who attains final release in the interval(43) One who attains final release on arrival(44) One who attains final release without effort(45) One who attains final release with effort(46) One who goes upstream to the Highest heaven(47) A stream-enterer(48) One practising to realize the fruit of stream-entry(49) A once-returner(50) One practising to realize the fruit of once-returning(51) A non-returner(52) One practising to realize the fruit of non-returning(53) An arahant(54) One practising to realize the fruit of arahantship [variant: arahattāya (Sī.)]Single Types.Two persons –(1) One who is angry, and one who holds grudges.(2) One who belittles others, and one who domineers [variant: palāsī (Syā., Ka.)].(3) One who is envious, and one who is stingy.(4) One who is crafty, and one who is deceitful.(5) One without conscience, and one without moral fear.(6) One who is hard to correct, and one who has bad friends.(7) One who does not guard the doors of the faculties, and one who lacks moderation in eating.(8) One who is forgetful, and one who is not clearly comprehending.(9) One who has failed in moral discipline, and one who has failed in view.(10) One with internal fetters, and one with external fetters.(11) One who is free of anger, and one who holds no grudges.(12) One who does not belittle others, and one who does not domineer.(13) One who is free of envy, and one who is free of stinginess.(14) One who is not crafty, and one who is not deceitful.(15) One who has conscience, and one who has moral fear.(16) One who is easy to correct, and one who has good friends.(17) One who guards the doors of the faculties, and one who has moderation in eating.(18) One whose mindfulness is established, and one who is clearly comprehending.(19) One accomplished in morality, and one accomplished in view.(20) Two persons are rare in the world.(21) Two persons are hard to satisfy.(22) Two persons are easy to satisfy.(23) For two persons, the taints grow.(24) For two persons, the taints do not grow.(25) One inclined to the inferior, and one inclined to the excellent.(26) One who is satisfied, and one who satisfies others.Pairs.Three persons –(1) One without hope, one with hope, and one whose hope is gone.(2) Three persons compared to sick people.(3) A body-witness, one attained to view, and one liberated by faith.(4) One whose speech is like dung, one whose speech is like flowers, and one whose speech is like honey.(5) A person whose mind is like an open sore, a person whose mind is like lightning, and a person whose mind is like a diamond.(6) One who is blind, one who is one-eyed, and one who is two-eyed.(7) A person whose wisdom is upturned, a person whose wisdom is like a lap [variant: uccaṅgupañño (Syā.)], and a person whose wisdom is wide.(8) There is someone who is not free of passion for sensual pleasures or for becoming; there is someone who is free of passion for sensual pleasures but not free of passion for becoming; there is someone who is free of passion for both sensual pleasures and becoming.(9) A person like a line drawn on rock, a person like a line drawn on earth, and a person like a line drawn on water.(10) Three persons compared to coarse cloth.(11) Three persons compared to fine Kāsi cloth.(12) One who is easy to measure, one who is hard to measure, and one who cannot be measured.(13) There is someone who should not be associated with, kept company with, or attended on; there is someone who should be associated with, kept company with, and attended on; there is someone who should be associated with, kept company with, and attended on with honour and respect [variant: garukatvā (Sī.)].(14) There is someone who should be shunned, and not associated with, kept company with, or attended on; there is someone who should be regarded with detachment, and not associated with, kept company with, or attended on; there is someone who should be associated with, kept company with, and attended on.(15) There is someone who fulfils morality [variant: paripūrīkārī (Syā.)], but practises concentration only to a limited degree and wisdom only to a limited degree; there is someone who fulfils morality and fulfils concentration, but practises wisdom only to a limited degree; there is someone who fulfils morality, fulfils concentration, and fulfils wisdom.(16) Three teachers.(17) Another three teachers.Threes.Four persons –(1) A bad person, one worse than a bad person, a good person, and one better than a good person.(2) One who is wicked, one more wicked than the wicked, one who is good, and one better than the good.(3) One of bad character, one worse than one of bad character, one of good character, and one better than one of good character.(4) One who is blameworthy, one with much blame, one with little blame [variant: appasāvajjo (Syā., Ka.) A. Ni. 4.135], and one who is blameless.(5) One who understands from a hint, one who understands after explanation [variant: vipacitaññū (Sī.) A. Ni. 4.133], one who must be guided, and one who gets no further than the words.(6) One whose ready understanding is apt but not fluent, one whose ready understanding is fluent but not apt, one whose ready understanding is both apt and fluent, and one whose ready understanding is neither apt nor fluent.(7) Four persons who teach the Teaching.(8) Four persons compared to rain clouds.(9) Four persons compared to mice.(10) Four persons compared to mangoes.(11) Four persons compared to pots.(12) Four persons compared to lakes.(13) Four persons compared to bulls [variant: balibaddūpamā (Sī.)].(14) Four persons compared to snakes.(15) There is someone who, without examining and without looking into it, praises one who deserves blame; there is someone who, without examining and without looking into it, blames one who deserves praise; there is someone who, without examining and without looking into it, shows trust where trust is not due; there is someone who, without examining and without looking into it, shows distrust where trust is due.(16) There is someone who, after examining and looking into it, blames one who deserves blame; there is someone who, after examining and looking into it, praises one who deserves praise; there is someone who, after examining and looking into it, shows distrust where trust is not due; there is someone who, after examining and looking into it, shows trust where trust is due.(17) There is someone who blames one who deserves blame, truthfully, accurately, at the right time, but does not praise one who deserves praise, truthfully, accurately, at the right time; there is someone who praises one who deserves praise, truthfully, accurately, at the right time, but does not blame one who deserves blame, truthfully, accurately, at the right time; there is someone who both blames one who deserves blame, truthfully, accurately, at the right time, and praises one who deserves praise, truthfully, accurately, at the right time; there is someone who neither blames one who deserves blame, truthfully, accurately, at the right time, nor praises one who deserves praise, truthfully, accurately, at the right time.(18) One who lives on the fruit of effort, not on the fruit of merit; one who lives on the fruit of merit, not on the fruit of effort; one who lives on both the fruit of effort and the fruit of merit; one who lives neither on the fruit of effort nor on the fruit of merit.(19) One in darkness headed for darkness, one in darkness headed for light, one in light headed for darkness, and one in light headed for light.(20) One sinking and sinking, one sinking and rising, one rising and sinking, and one rising and rising.(21) Four persons compared to trees.(22) One who judges by appearance and is won over by appearance, and one who judges by voice and is won over by voice.(23) One who judges by plainness and is won over by plainness, and one who judges by spiritual qualities and is won over by spiritual qualities.(24) There is someone who works for their own welfare, not for the welfare of others; there is someone who works for the welfare of others, not for their own welfare; there is someone who works both for their own welfare and for the welfare of others; there is someone who works neither for their own welfare nor for the welfare of others.(25) There is someone who torments themselves, devoted to the practice of tormenting themselves; there is someone who torments others, devoted to the practice of tormenting others; there is someone who both torments themselves, devoted to the practice of tormenting themselves, and torments others, devoted to the practice of tormenting others; there is someone who neither torments themselves nor is devoted to the practice of tormenting themselves, and neither torments others nor is devoted to the practice of tormenting others. Not tormenting themselves and not tormenting others, they live in this very life free from hunger, at peace, cooled [variant: sītibhūto (Sī., Ka.)], experiencing happiness, having themselves become holy.(26) One with lust, one with hatred, one with delusion, and one with conceit.(27) There is someone who gains internal calm of mind but not insight into things through higher wisdom; there is someone who gains insight into things through higher wisdom but not internal calm of mind; there is someone who gains both internal calm of mind and insight into things through higher wisdom; there is someone who gains neither internal calm of mind nor insight into things through higher wisdom.(28) A person who goes with the stream, a person who goes against the stream, a person who stands firm, and the brahmin who has crossed over, reached the far shore [variant: pāragato (Sī., Syā.)], and stands on land.(29) One with little learning who does not live up to their learning, one with little learning who lives up to their learning, one with much learning who does not live up to their learning, and one with much learning who lives up to their learning.(30) The unshakable ascetic, the red-lotus ascetic, the white-lotus ascetic, and the refined ascetic among ascetics.Fours.Five persons –(1) There is someone who does wrong [variant: ārambhati (Sī., Syā.)] and feels remorse, and does not really understand that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom in which those bad, unwholesome states that have arisen in them cease without remainder. There is someone who does wrong but does not feel remorse, and does not really understand that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom in which those bad, unwholesome states that have arisen in them cease without remainder. There is someone who does no wrong but feels remorse, and does not really understand that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom in which those bad, unwholesome states that have arisen in them cease without remainder. There is someone who does no wrong and does not feel remorse, and does not really understand that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom in which those bad, unwholesome states that have arisen in them cease without remainder. There is someone who does no wrong and does not feel remorse, and really understands that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom in which those bad, unwholesome states that have arisen in them cease without remainder.(2) One who gives and then looks down on others, one who looks down on others through living with them, one who believes too readily, one who is fickle, and one who is dull and confused.(3) Five persons compared to warriors.(4) Five who eat only alms food.(5) Five who refuse food offered later.(6) Five who eat at one sitting.(7) Five who wear robes made of rags.(8) Five who use only three robes.(9) Five forest dwellers.(10) Five who live at the foot of a tree.(11) Five who live in the open air.(12) Five who never lie down.(13) Five who accept whatever place is assigned.(14) Five who live in charnel grounds.Fives.Six persons –(1) There is someone who, in teachings not heard before, awakens to the truths by themselves, and attains there all-knowing wisdom and mastery of the powers [variant: phalesu (Pī.)]. There is someone who, in teachings not heard before, awakens to the truths by themselves, but does not attain there all-knowing wisdom or mastery of the powers. There is someone who, in teachings not heard before, does not awaken to the truths by themselves, but makes an end of suffering in this very life and attains the perfection of a disciple. There is someone who, in teachings not heard before, does not awaken to the truths by themselves, but makes an end of suffering in this very life, though they do not attain the perfection of a disciple. There is someone who, in teachings not heard before, does not awaken to the truths by themselves, and does not make an end of suffering in this very life, but is a non-returner who does not come back [variant: anāgantvā (Syā., Ka.) A. Ni. 4.171] to this state of existence. There is someone who, in teachings not heard before, does not awaken to the truths by themselves, and does not make an end of suffering in this very life, but is a returner [variant: sotāpannasakadāgāmī (Syā., Ka.)] who comes back to this state of existence.Sixes.Seven persons –(1) Seven persons compared to people in water. One who has sunk once stays sunk; one who comes up and sinks again; one who comes up and stays established; one who comes up, sees clearly and looks around; one who comes up and swims across; one who comes up and attains a foothold; one who comes up, has crossed over, reached the far shore, and stands on land – the brahmin.(2) One liberated both ways, one liberated by wisdom, a body-witness, one attained to view, one liberated by faith, a follower by the teaching, and a follower by faith.Sevens.Eight persons –(1) The four persons who possess the path, and the four persons who possess the fruit.Eights.Nine persons –(1) A Fully Awakened Buddha, a Solitary Buddha, one liberated both ways, one liberated by wisdom, a body-witness, one attained to view, one liberated by faith, a follower by the teaching, and a follower by faith.Nines.Ten persons –(1) For five, the goal is reached here; for five, the goal is reached after leaving here.Tens.The matrix of the Description of Persons is complete.What kind of person is one liberated at times? Here, someone lives from time to time, on occasion after occasion, having touched [variant: phassitvā (Sī., Pī.)] the eight liberations with the body, and, having seen with wisdom, some of their taints are destroyed – this person is called "one liberated at times".What kind of person is one liberated regardless of times? Here, someone does not live from time to time, on occasion after occasion, having touched the eight liberations with the body, yet, having seen with wisdom, their taints are destroyed – this person is called "one liberated regardless of times". All noble persons are liberated regardless of times with respect to the noble liberation.What kind of person is one whose attainments can be shaken? Here, someone has gained the meditative attainments connected with form or with the formless. But they have not gained them at will, without trouble, without difficulty; they do not enter them and emerge from them wherever they wish, whichever they wish, and for as long as they wish. It is possible that, through heedlessness, those attainments of that person may be shaken – this person is called "one whose attainments can be shaken".What kind of person is one whose attainments cannot be shaken? Here, someone has gained the meditative attainments connected with form or with the formless. And they have gained them at will, without trouble, without difficulty; they enter them and emerge from them wherever they wish, whichever they wish, and for as long as they wish. It is impossible, it cannot happen, that, through heedlessness, those attainments of that person should be shaken – this person is called "one whose attainments cannot be shaken". All noble persons have attainments that cannot be shaken with respect to the noble liberation.What kind of person is one liable to fall away? Here, someone has gained the meditative attainments connected with form or with the formless. But they have not gained them at will, without trouble, without difficulty; they do not enter them and emerge from them wherever they wish, whichever they wish, and for as long as they wish. It is possible that, through heedlessness, that person may fall away from those attainments – this person is called "one liable to fall away".What kind of person is one not liable to fall away? Here, someone has gained the meditative attainments connected with form or with the formless. And they have gained them at will, without trouble, without difficulty; they enter them and emerge from them wherever they wish, whichever they wish, and for as long as they wish. It is impossible, it cannot happen, that, through heedlessness, that person should fall away from those attainments – this person is called "one not liable to fall away". All noble persons are not liable to fall away with respect to the noble liberation.What kind of person is one able to hold on through volition? Here, someone has gained the meditative attainments connected with form or with the formless. But they have not gained them at will, without trouble, without difficulty; they do not enter them and emerge from them wherever they wish, whichever they wish, and for as long as they wish. If they keep their intent on them, they do not fall away from those attainments. If they do not keep their intent on them, they fall away from those attainments – this person is called "one able to hold on through volition".What kind of person is one able to hold on through guarding? Here, someone has gained the meditative attainments connected with form or with the formless. But they have not gained them at will, without trouble, without difficulty; they do not enter them and emerge from them wherever they wish, whichever they wish, and for as long as they wish. If they guard them, they do not fall away from those attainments. If they do not guard them, they fall away from those attainments – this person is called "one able to hold on through guarding".What kind of person is an ordinary person? The person whose three fetters are not abandoned, and who is not practising to abandon those states – this person is called "an ordinary person".What kind of person is one who enters the lineage? The person who possesses those states immediately after which the noble state comes about – this person is called "one who enters the lineage".What kind of person is one who refrains out of fear? The seven learners, and those ordinary persons who are virtuous, refrain out of fear. An arahant refrains without fear.What kind of person is one unable to progress? Those persons who are hindered by their actions, hindered by defilements, hindered by results, who are without faith, without zeal, lacking wisdom, and dull, unable to enter the course of rightness in wholesome states – these persons are called "those unable to progress".What kind of person is one able to progress? Those persons who are not hindered by their actions, not hindered by defilements, not hindered by results, who have faith, have zeal, are wise [variant: paññavantā (Sī.)], and are not dull, able to enter the course of rightness in wholesome states – these persons are called "those able to progress".What kind of person is one whose destiny is fixed? The five persons who have done deeds with immediate results, those with wrong view whose destiny is fixed, and the eight noble persons are persons whose destiny is fixed. The remaining persons are persons whose destiny is not fixed.What kind of person is one who is practising? The four persons who possess the path are those who are practising; the four persons who possess the fruit are established in the fruit.What kind of person is one whose two ends come at once? The person for whom the ending of the taints and the ending of life occur neither earlier nor later than each other – this person is called "one whose two ends come at once".What kind of person is one for whom the aeon remains? Suppose this person were practising to realize the fruit of stream-entry, and it were the time for the aeon to burn up: the aeon would not burn up until this person had realized the fruit of stream-entry. This person is called "one for whom the aeon remains". All persons who possess the path are ones for whom the aeon remains.What kind of person is a noble one? The eight noble persons are noble. The remaining persons are not noble.What kind of person is a learner? The four persons who possess the path and the three persons who possess the fruit are "learners". An arahant is an adept. The remaining persons are neither learners nor adepts.What kind of person is one with the three knowledges? A person who possesses the three knowledges is "one with the three knowledges".What kind of person is one with the six direct knowledges? A person who possesses the six direct knowledges is "one with the six direct knowledges".What kind of person is a Fully Awakened Buddha? Here, someone, in teachings not heard before, awakens to the truths by themselves; and attains there all-knowing wisdom and mastery of the powers – this person is called "a Fully Awakened Buddha".What kind of person is a Solitary Buddha? Here, someone, in teachings not heard before, awakens to the truths by themselves; but does not attain there all-knowing wisdom, nor mastery of the powers – this person is called "a Solitary Buddha".What kind of person is one liberated both ways? Here, someone lives having touched the eight liberations with the body; and, having seen with wisdom, their taints are destroyed – this person is called "one liberated both ways".What kind of person is one liberated by wisdom? Here, someone does not live having touched the eight liberations with the body; yet, having seen with wisdom, their taints are destroyed. This person is called "one liberated by wisdom".What kind of person is a body-witness? Here, someone lives having touched the eight liberations with the body; and, having seen with wisdom, some of their taints are destroyed. This person is called "a body-witness".What kind of person is one attained to view? Here, someone really understands, "This is suffering"; really understands, "This is the origin of suffering"; really understands, "This is the cessation of suffering"; really understands, "This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering". And the teachings proclaimed by the Tathāgata have been clearly seen and examined by them with wisdom. And, having seen with wisdom, some of their taints are destroyed – this person is called "one attained to view".What kind of person is one liberated by faith? Here, someone really understands, "This is suffering"; really understands, "This is the origin of suffering"; really understands, "This is the cessation of suffering"; really understands, "This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering". And the teachings proclaimed by the Tathāgata have been clearly seen and examined by them with wisdom. And, having seen with wisdom, some of their taints are destroyed, but not in the way they are for one attained to view – this person is called "one liberated by faith".What kind of person is a follower by the teaching? The person who is practising to realize the fruit of stream-entry, in whom the wisdom faculty is predominant, and who cultivates the noble path that is carried by wisdom and led by wisdom – this person is called "a follower by the teaching". A person practising to realize the fruit of stream-entry is a follower by the teaching; once established in the fruit, they are one attained to view.What kind of person is a follower by faith? The person who is practising to realize the fruit of stream-entry, in whom the faith faculty is predominant, and who cultivates the noble path that is carried by faith and led by faith – this person is called "a follower by faith". A person practising to realize the fruit of stream-entry is a follower by faith; once established in the fruit, they are one liberated by faith.What kind of person is one with at most seven more lives? Here, someone, through the complete destruction of three fetters, is a stream-enterer, no longer liable to fall into the lower realms, fixed in destiny, and headed for awakening [variant: sambodhiparāyaṇo (Sī., Ka.)]. After running on and wandering among gods and humans seven times, they make an end of suffering – this person is called "one with at most seven more lives".What kind of person is one who goes from family to family? Here, someone, through the complete destruction of three fetters, is a stream-enterer, no longer liable to fall into the lower realms, fixed in destiny, and headed for awakening. After running on and wandering through two or three families, they make an end of suffering – this person is called "one who goes from family to family".What kind of person is one with a single seed? Here, someone, through the complete destruction of three fetters, is a stream-enterer, no longer liable to fall into the lower realms, fixed in destiny, and headed for awakening. After producing just one human becoming, they make an end of suffering – this person is called "one with a single seed".What kind of person is a once-returner? Here, someone, through the complete destruction of three fetters and the weakening of lust, hatred and delusion, is a once-returner; coming back to this world only once more, they make an end of suffering – this person is called "a once-returner".What kind of person is a non-returner? Here, someone, through the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, is reborn spontaneously; they attain final release there, and are not liable to return from that world – this person is called "a non-returner".What kind of person is one who attains final release in the interval? Here, someone, through the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, is reborn spontaneously; they attain final release there, and are not liable to return from that world. Either immediately after being reborn, or before reaching the middle of their lifespan, they bring forth the noble path for abandoning the higher fetters – this person is called "one who attains final release in the interval".What kind of person is one who attains final release on arrival? Here, someone, through the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, is reborn spontaneously; they attain final release there, and are not liable to return from that world. After passing the middle of their lifespan, or on the arrival of death [variant: kālaṃ kiriyaṃ (Ka.)], they bring forth the noble path for abandoning the higher fetters – this person is called "one who attains final release on arrival".What kind of person is one who attains final release without effort? Here, someone, through the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, is reborn spontaneously; they attain final release there, and are not liable to return from that world. Without effort, they bring forth the noble path for abandoning the higher fetters – this person is called "one who attains final release without effort".What kind of person is one who attains final release with effort? Here, someone, through the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, is reborn spontaneously; they attain final release there, and are not liable to return from that world. With effort, they bring forth the noble path for abandoning the higher fetters – this person is called "one who attains final release with effort".What kind of person is one who goes upstream to the Highest heaven? Here, someone, through the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, is reborn spontaneously; they attain final release there, and are not liable to return from that world. Passing away from the Aviha heaven, they go to the Atappa heaven; passing away from the Atappa heaven, they go to the Sudassa heaven; passing away from the Sudassa heaven, they go to the Sudassī heaven; passing away from the Sudassī heaven, they go to the Highest heaven; in the Highest heaven they bring forth the noble path for abandoning the higher fetters – this person is called "one who goes upstream to the Highest heaven".What kind of person is a stream-enterer, and one practising to realize the fruit of stream-entry? A person practising to abandon the three fetters is one practising to realize the fruit of stream-entry. The person whose three fetters are abandoned – this person is called "a stream-enterer".A person practising to weaken sensual lust and ill will is one practising to realize the fruit of once-returning. The person whose sensual lust and ill will are weakened – this person is called "a once-returner".A person practising to abandon sensual lust and ill will without remainder is one practising to realize the fruit of non-returning. The person whose sensual lust and ill will are abandoned without remainder – this person is called "a non-returner".A person practising to abandon without remainder lust for form, lust for the formless, conceit, restlessness and ignorance is one practising to realize the fruit of arahantship. The person whose lust for form, lust for the formless, conceit, restlessness and ignorance are abandoned without remainder – this person is called "an arahant".End of the exposition of single types.What kind of person is one who is angry? In this context, what is anger? Whatever anger there is, being angry, angriness, hatred, hating, hatefulness [variant: dūsanā dūsitattaṃ (Syā.)], ill will, ill-willed bearing, being ill-willed, hostility, antagonism, fierceness, abusiveness, displeasure of consciousness – this is called anger. The person in whom this anger is not abandoned – this person is called "one who is angry".What kind of person is one who holds grudges? In this context, what is resentment? First there is anger, later there is resentment. Whatever resentment of this kind there is, bearing a grudge, being resentful, not letting go [variant: āṭhapanā (Ka.) Vibha. 891], keeping, fixing, joining, prolonging, strengthening of anger – this is called resentment. The person in whom this resentment is not abandoned – this person is called "one who holds grudges".What kind of person is one who belittles others? In this context, what is belittling? Whatever belittling there is, acting belittlingly, the state of belittling [variant: makkhīyanā makkhīyitattaṃ (Sī.), makkhiyanā makkhiyitattaṃ (Ka.)], callousness, callous behaviour – this is called belittling. These are the five who live in charnel grounds.End of the exposition of fives.Of these, the person who, in teachings not heard before, awakens to the truths by themselves, and attains there all-knowing wisdom and mastery of the powers – this should be understood to mean a Fully Awakened Buddha.Of these, the person who, in teachings not heard before, awakens to the truths by themselves, but does not attain there all-knowing wisdom or mastery of the powers – this should be understood to mean a Solitary Buddha.Of these, the person who, in teachings not heard before, does not awaken to the truths by themselves, but makes an end of suffering in this very life [variant: dukkhassantaṃ karoti (Sī.); likewise further on] and attains the perfection of a disciple – this should be understood to mean Sāriputta and Moggallāna.Of these, the person who, in teachings not heard before, does not awaken to the truths by themselves, but makes an end of suffering in this very life, though they do not attain the perfection of a disciple – this should be understood to mean the remaining arahants.Of these, the person who, in teachings not heard before, does not awaken to the truths by themselves, and does not make an end of suffering in this very life, but is a non-returner who does not come back to this state of existence – this should be understood to mean a non-returner.Of these, the person who, in teachings not heard before, does not awaken to the truths by themselves, and does not make an end of suffering in this very life, but comes back to this state of existence – this should be understood to mean stream-enterers and once-returners.End of the exposition of sixes.And how is a person one who has sunk once and stays sunk? Here, someone possesses unwholesome states that are entirely black. In this way a person is one who has sunk once and stays sunk.And how is a person one who comes up and sinks again? Here, someone comes up, thinking: "Faith in wholesome states is good, conscience in wholesome states is good [variant: sāhu (Sī., Syā.); likewise in all three places], moral fear in wholesome states is good, energy [variant: viriyaṃ (Sī., Syā.)] in wholesome states is good, wisdom in wholesome states is good." But their faith neither stays nor grows; it only declines. Their conscience neither stays nor grows; it only declines. Their moral fear neither stays nor grows; it only declines. Their energy neither stays nor grows; it only declines. Their wisdom neither stays nor grows; it only declines. In this way a person is one who comes up and sinks again.And how is a person one who comes up and stays established? Here, someone comes up, thinking: "Faith in wholesome states is good, conscience in wholesome states is good, moral fear in wholesome states is good, energy in wholesome states is good, wisdom in wholesome states is good." Their faith neither declines nor grows; it stays established. Their conscience neither declines nor grows; it stays established. Their moral fear neither declines nor grows; it stays established. Their energy neither declines nor grows; it stays established. Their wisdom neither declines nor grows; it stays established. In this way a person is one who comes up and stays established.And how is a person one who comes up, sees clearly and looks around? Here, someone comes up, thinking: "Faith in wholesome states is good, conscience in wholesome states is good, moral fear in wholesome states is good, energy in wholesome states is good, wisdom in wholesome states is good." Through the complete destruction of three fetters, they are a stream-enterer, no longer liable to fall into the lower realms, fixed in destiny, and headed for awakening. In this way a person is one who comes up, sees clearly and looks around.And how is a person one who comes up and swims across? Here, someone comes up, thinking: "Faith in wholesome states is good, conscience in wholesome states is good, moral fear in wholesome states is good, energy in wholesome states is good, wisdom in wholesome states is good." Through the complete destruction of three fetters and the weakening of lust, hatred and delusion, they are a once-returner; coming back to this world only once more, they make an end of suffering. In this way a person is one who comes up and swims across.And how is a person one who comes up and attains a foothold? Here, someone comes up, thinking: "Faith in wholesome states is good, conscience in wholesome states is good, moral fear in wholesome states is good, energy in wholesome states is good, wisdom in wholesome states is good." Through the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, they are reborn spontaneously; they attain final release there, and are not liable to return from that world. In this way a person is one who comes up and attains a foothold.And how is a person one who comes up and is the brahmin who has crossed over, reached the far shore and stands on land? Here, someone comes up, thinking: "Faith in wholesome states is good, conscience in wholesome states is good, moral fear in wholesome states is good, energy in wholesome states is good, wisdom in wholesome states is good." Through the destruction of the taints, they have realized by direct knowledge themselves, in this very life, the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom that is free of taints, and live having entered it. In this way a person is one who comes up and is the brahmin who has crossed over, reached the far shore and stands on land.What kind of person is one liberated both ways? Here, someone lives having touched the eight liberations with the body, and, having seen with wisdom, their taints are destroyed. This person is called one liberated both ways.What kind of person is one liberated by wisdom … a body-witness … one attained to view … one liberated by faith … a follower by the teaching ….What kind of person is a follower by faith? The person who is practising to realize the fruit of stream-entry, in whom the faith faculty is predominant, and who cultivates the noble path that is carried by faith and led by faith. This person is called a follower by faith. A person practising to realize the fruit of stream-entry is a follower by faith; once established in the fruit, they are one liberated by faith.End of the exposition of sevens.In this context, what are the four persons who possess the path and the four persons who possess the fruit? A stream-enterer, and one practising to realize the fruit of stream-entry; a once-returner, and one practising to realize the fruit of once-returning; a non-returner, and one practising to realize the fruit of non-returning; an arahant, and one practising to realize the fruit of arahantship [variant: arahattāya (Syā., Ka.) A. Ni. 8.59]; these are the four persons who possess the path, and these are the four persons who possess the fruit.End of the exposition of eights.What kind of person is a Fully Awakened Buddha? Here, someone, in teachings not heard before, awakens to the truths by themselves, and attains there all-knowing wisdom and mastery of the powers. This person is called a Fully Awakened Buddha.What kind of person is a Solitary Buddha? Here, someone, in teachings not heard before, awakens to the truths by themselves, but does not attain there all-knowing wisdom, nor mastery of the powers. This person is called a Solitary Buddha.What kind of person is one liberated both ways? Here, someone lives having touched the eight liberations with the body, and, having seen with wisdom, their taints are destroyed. This person is called one liberated both ways.What kind of person is one liberated by wisdom? Here, someone does not live having touched the eight liberations with the body, yet, having seen with wisdom, their taints are destroyed. This person is called one liberated by wisdom.What kind of person is a body-witness? Here, someone lives having touched the eight liberations with the body, and, having seen with wisdom, some of their taints are destroyed. This person is called a body-witness.What kind of person is one attained to view? Here, someone really understands, "This is suffering" … really understands, "This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering". The teachings proclaimed by the Tathāgata have been clearly seen and examined by them with wisdom, and, having seen with wisdom, some of their taints are destroyed. This person is called one attained to view.What kind of person is one liberated by faith? Here, someone really understands, "This is suffering" … really understands, "This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering". The teachings proclaimed by the Tathāgata have been clearly seen and examined by them with wisdom, and, having seen with wisdom, some of their taints are destroyed, but not in the way they are for one attained to view. This person is called one liberated by faith.What kind of person is a follower by the teaching? The person who is practising to realize the fruit of stream-entry, in whom the wisdom faculty is predominant, and who cultivates the noble path that is carried by wisdom and led by wisdom. This person is called a follower by the teaching. A person practising to realize the fruit of stream-entry is a follower by the teaching; once established in the fruit, they are one attained to view.What kind of person is a follower by faith? The person who is practising to realize the fruit of stream-entry, in whom the faith faculty is predominant, and who cultivates the noble path that is carried by faith and led by faith. This person is called a follower by faith. A person practising to realize the fruit of stream-entry is a follower by faith; once established in the fruit, they are one liberated by faith.End of the exposition of nines.For which five is the goal reached here? For one with at most seven more lives, one who goes from family to family, one with a single seed, a once-returner, and whoever is an arahant in this very life – for these five, the goal is reached here.For which five is the goal reached after leaving here? For one who attains final release in the interval, one who attains final release on arrival, one who attains final release without effort, one who attains final release with effort, and one who goes upstream to the Highest heaven – for these five, the goal is reached after leaving here.That is what the description of persons covers.End of the exposition of tens.The treatise, the Description of Persons, is complete.
